header.title: Descriptio Consulum Ex Quo Primum Ordinati Sunt [Codex Parisiensis]: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Idatius Aquaeflaviensis Episcopus
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's stoa0154a.stoa002.opp-lat1, from Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. The whole work is translated. It was chosen because no English translation of it could be found.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation of the whole work, checked against the original by a second AI only in samples. No specialist has reviewed it.
header.availability: CC BY-SA 4.0, as its source requires: credit Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina and this AI translation, and share adaptations under the same licence.

notes.urn:cts:latinLit:stoa0154a.stoa002.opp-l: Names are given in the nominative; the list has them in the ablative of dating ('in the consulship of'). Bracketed variants and 'perhaps: without consuls' are the editor's notes, not the list's. Several year numbers misread in the scan have been corrected from the sequence (e.g. 362→262, 260→269, 295→293, 500→300, 502→302, 505→303, 506→306, 508→308, 525→325). Line 21: 'His tonsa' is evidently corrupt, probably for 'His conss.' ('in their consulship'), and is translated that way; the sense of the notice is obscure. Line 86: 'In' stands where a year number should be, presumably a misread figure, so it is given as [...]. Line 78 shows a year (331) run into the previous entry. In line 166 'Domino' was taken as Domitius; this is uncertain. Many name forms in the list are corrupt (e.g. Politus for Potitus, Roeticus for Peticus, Venox for Venno) and are kept as the list gives them.

Year numbers misprinted in the scan have been corrected from the sequence: 590 to 490, 5f8 to 518, 53! to 531, 557 to 537, 656 to 636. 502: 'Coita' read as Cotta, as in 506. 504: 'Vne' is unclear and probably corrupt; the colleague of Regulus II in this year was L. Manlius Vulso. 514: the Cicero reference is printed '7i', taken as Brutus 72. 526: 'Vcro' is unclear, perhaps an abbreviation of Verrucosus. 550: '$0' read as 60. 607, 609, 633: 'Aemilii' (literally 'of Aemilius') is left as printed; the variant gives the cognomen Aemilianus. 672: 'Maria' read as Marius. 675: 'Valia' read as Vatia (P. Servilius Vatia). 592: 'vilio' read as vitio, 'with a flaw', i.e. a defect in the auspices.

Many evident scanning errors corrected silently (e.g. 609 for 699, Scipiont, Saturoino, Lenlulo, Camille, 47 for 17, 59 for 39, Jodæu for Judaea, tUo for Tito, iteration numerals misread as 'n', 'm', 'It', 'tv'). 744: the editor's bracket is garbled and unclosed ('[Al. Fab. M. Afric. et I Antonio'); rendered as far as legible, 'I.' probably for Iullus. 21: the variant '[Al. Drus. Tibi at. II]' is garbled; read as 'Drus. Tib. f. II' (Drusus son of Tiberius, second time), uncertain. 3 'Servilio niano' and 33 'Galba libolo' are fragmentary in the manuscript ('Sic ms.'); left as fragments. 721 'Æra prima' is ambiguous; taken as the first year of the Spanish Era.

Year numbers misprinted in the scan have been corrected from the sequence: '417' to 117, '435' to 135, '210' to 220, 'I 211' to 211, and 'Hi' to 222. At 212, "Duobus 'april" is read as 'Duobus Aspris', 'the two Aspri'. At 258, 'Ivm kal. Octobris' is read as XVIII Kal. Oct. (14 September). At 123, 'Aproniainus' in the English should read 'Aproniainus' → 'Aproniainus' is a typing slip for Aproniainus/Aproniainus = Aproniainus; the Latin is Aproniano, i.e. Aproniainus. The line after 167 is a fragmentary editorial or manuscript remark: the names of those who suffered are missing. At 200, '[Male n]' is taken as 'wrongly II'. At 261, 'Romania' means Roman territory.

Several year numbers and Spanish Era figures in the scan are misprinted and have been corrected (305→303 at 753; 530, 532, 355, 557 → 330, 332, 333, 337; Spanish Era 560 and 580 → 360 and 380). 294: 'contra Acinco et Donomia' read as opposite Aquincum and Bononia. 302: 'vilitatem ... esse' taken as an order for low prices (the price edict). 307–310: 'Novies', 'Decies' refer to Maximian's ninth and tenth consulships; the dating formulas are confused in the manuscript and are rendered literally. 335: the lemma reads 'Constantino [Al. Constantio]'; the consul was Julius Constantius. 342: 'tractus Hermogenes' means Hermogenes was dragged [to death]. 346, 352–361: the manuscript reads 'Constantino' in places where Constantius is meant, and these have been rendered as Constantius. 351: 'Morsa' is Mursa. 357: 'edidit XXXV' is taken as celebrating his thirty-fifth anniversary (tricennalia+); the sense is uncertain. 359: Gratian's birth year is misplaced in the source. 360: 'Dominicum' is taken as the Great Church. 361: 'Ciliciae Phoeniciae provinciae' is rendered as the text gives it, but it is geographically confused. 314: 'bellum Cibalense' is the battle of Cibalae, which in fact took place in 316.

Many scanning errors corrected silently (e.g. 'erret. sum' = egressum, 'iam' = intra, '333/S78/593/594/596/598/599/391' for 383/378/393/394/396/398/399/397, 'Cautone' = Bautone, 'Virgitione' = Brigetio, 'Acinco' = Aquincum, 'Auico' = Attico, 'Rumorido', 'Varari' = Varane). 366: the text repeats 'campos ab A' (dittography). 369: 'Agon post anno XVII restitutus est ali Augusto Valente' is garbled; rendered as 'after seventeen years the contest was restored by Augustus Valens'. 383: the manuscript names Constantia as daughter of Constantine; she was daughter of Constantius II. 388: 'neu' read as luctu/maerore ('grief'); the date 'xxv kal. April.' is impossible as written (no such day) and is likely corrupt; stray 'B' before 'tyrannus' omitted. 393: the second consul (Abundantius) is missing in the text. 405: the Donatist notice stands as a separate line in the edition. 410: 'quod fuit Tertullo' is obscure; possibly referring to Tertullus, consul under Attalus. 411: 'Constantini' in the text; 'Constantino II' in 417 corrected to Constantius by context (Constantius III in 420).

Line 423: 'recessit' is taken in its late sense 'died'; 'Ravenna' as locative. Line 445: the editor's parenthesis is left unfinished in the source; the year-numbers from here on are misaligned with the true consulships, as the editor's notes indicate. Line 431 (second) is evidently 434. Line 464: the notices (death of Severus 465, Anthemius 467, Vandal expedition 468) belong to later years; the jump to 468 follows the source. 'Pierio et Artabu' and 'Gadaipho' are kept as the manuscript's forms, with the variants given.

nodes.text: THE LIST OF CONSULS OF BISHOP HYDATIUS, FROM THE TIME WHEN THEY WERE FIRST APPOINTED. From a manuscript of the library of the Paris college of the Society of Jesus. Labbe added the Varronian years from the founding of the City in the margin.
247 Publicola for the 2nd time and Publilius [another reading: Pulvillus].
250 Publicola for the 3rd time and Lucretius for the 2nd time.
260 Caelimontanus for the 2nd time and Vitellinus for the 3rd time [another reading: Geminus for the 2nd time].
261 Auruncus for the 2nd time and Vitellinus.
263 Augurinus for the 2nd time and Atratinus.
265 Tallus [another reading: Julus] and Ruffus. In their consulship the Roman leading men were named.
266 Nautius and Rufus [another reading: Fusus or Furius].
272 Tertullus [another reading: Julus] and Fabius for the 2nd time.
274 Cincinnatus and Fabius for the 3rd time.
275 Rutilius and Fabius for the 4th time.
276 Aemilius for the 2nd time and Aesculinus [another reading: Esquilinus].
277 Laenas and Publilius [another reading: Lautus and Pulvillus].
285 Caelimontanus and Priscus for the 2nd time.
287 Aemilius for the 2nd time and Vibulanus.
289 Omitted: Capitolinus for the 3rd time and Fabius for the 2nd time.
294 Publicola for the 2nd time and Sabinus.
297 Publilius and Hilarius [another reading: Pulvillus and Augurinus].
300 Capitolinus and Varus [another reading: Aeternius or Aterius].
302 Laenas and Capitolinus. In their consulship [perhaps: without consuls] the decemvirs were created, the first and the second, for 2 years.
309 Genucius and Curtius. In their consulship three tribunes of the plebs were made, for 1 year.
315 Maltius [another reading: Menenius] and Capitolinus. In their consulship [perhaps: without consuls] likewise three tribunes of the plebs, for 2 years.
320 Capitolinus and Camerinus. In their consulship [perhaps: without consuls] likewise three tribunes of the plebs, for 2 years.
325 Tricipitinus and Fidenas for the 2nd time.
327 Achilla [another reading: Ahala] and Mugillanus. In their consulship [perhaps: without consuls] likewise three tribunes of the plebs, for 3 years. 331 Atratinus and Vibulanus.
332 Capitolinus and Vibulanus. In their consulship [perhaps: without consuls] likewise four tribunes of the plebs, for 8 years.
344 Aemilius and Rusticus [another reading: C. Valerius].
345 Cossus and Medullinus. In their consulship [perhaps: without consuls] likewise tribunes of the plebs, 4, and 2, and 6, for 15 years.

[...] Potitus and Capitolinus. In their consulship [perhaps: without consuls] likewise tribunes of the plebs were created for 18 years, afterwards for 4 years; there was no curule magistrate. Likewise 6 tribunes of the plebs.
388 Mamertinus [another reading: Mamercus, or Mamercinus] and Lateranus.
391 Mamertinus for the 2nd time and Silla [another reading: Genucius].
395 Libo [another reading: Manlius; see Sigonius] and Laenas.
400 Omitted: Ambustus for the 3rd time and Capitolinus.
401 Missing: Peticus for the 4th time and Poplicola for the 2nd time.
402 Missing: P. Publicola and Rutilus for the 2nd time.
403 Roeticus and Poenus [another reading: Peticus and Pennus].
404 Scipio and Laenas for the 2nd time.
406 Corvinus and Laenas for the 3rd time.
408 Corvinus for the 2nd time and Libo.
410 Rutilus and Torquatus for the 2nd time.
411 Corvinus for the 3rd time and Cossus.
412 Ahala and Rutilus for the 2nd time.
413 Venox [another reading: Venno] for the 2nd time and Mamertinus.
414 Torquatus for the 3rd time and Muso [another reading: Mus].
420 Albinus and Galbinus [another reading: Calvinus]. See Sigonius.
425 Mamertinus for the 2nd time and Decianus.
426 Venox for the 2nd time and Scipio.
428 Libonius [another reading: Libo] and Cursor. 429 Camillus and Brutus.
In their consulship [perhaps: without consuls] Papirius Cursor was then created dictator, and Drusus master of horse.
432 Cursor and Rullus [another reading: Max. Rullianus and Fulvius Curvus].
434 Cursor for the 2nd time and Philo.
436 Venox and Flaccinus [another reading: Venno and Flaccus].
439 Cursor for the 3rd time and Laenas [another reading: Philo] for the 2nd time.
441 Cursor for the 4th time and Bubulcus for the 2nd time.
443 Bubulcus for the 3rd time and Barbula.
444 Rullus and Rutilius. In their consulship [perhaps: without consuls] Cursor was then dictator, and Bubulcus master of horse.
446 Muso [another reading: Mus] for the 2nd time and Rullus for the 2nd time.
447 Appius Caecus and Violens [another reading: Volumnius].
449 Metellus [another reading: Megellus] and Minucius. 450 Sempronius and Faberius [another reading: Saverrio or Averrio].
452 Dento [another reading: Denter] and Aemilius. In their consulship [perhaps: without consuls] Corvinus was dictator, and Aemilius master of horse, for 6 months; then there were [consuls].
455 Paeticus [another reading: Paetinus or Paetus] and Torquatus.
457 Rullus for the 3rd time and Muso for the 3rd time [another reading: Q. Fabius for the 4th time and P. Decius for the 3rd time].

458 Claudius and Violens [another reading: Volumnius for the 2nd time]. Rullus for the 4th time and Muso for the 4th time. Claudius for the 2nd time and Violens for the 2nd time. (These seem to have been wrongly inserted.)
459 Rullus for the 5th time and Muso for the 5th time [another reading: 4th].
460 Metellus [another reading: Megellus for the 2nd time] and Regulus.
462 Maximus Gurges and Bracchus [another reading: Brutus].
463 Metellus for the 2nd time and Vulbus [another reading: Megellus for the 3rd time and Bubulcus].
470 Dacius and Dento [another reading: Tucca and Denter].
475 Caverio and Muso [another reading: Saverrio and Mus].
480 Dentatus for the 2nd time [another reading: 3rd] and Merenda.
484 Omitted: Clepsina for the 2nd time and Blasio.
485 Gallus Sabinus and Piso [another reading: Pictor].
488 Fabius Pictor and Poeta [another reading: Pera].
492 Albinus [another reading: L. Postumius Megellus] and Vitulus.
493 Flaccus for the 2nd time and Crassus.
498 Vulso and Decius [another reading: Caedicius], in whose place Regulus was substituted.
504 Regulus for the 2nd time and Vne.
506 Cotta for the 2nd time and Geminus for the 2nd time.
509 Buteo for the 2nd time and Bullus [another reading: Balbus].
515 Tuncinus and Falco [another reading: Turrinus and Falto].
518 Claudius Lentulus [another reading: P. Cornelius Lentulus Caudinus] and Varus.
524 Barbula for the 2nd time and Pera.
526 Burga and Maximus Vcro [another reading: Q. Fabius Maximus and Carvilius].
527 Flaccus and Regulus (Cicero, On Old Age, 11).
528 Maximus Messala [another reading: Valerius Messala] and Apustius.
533 Scipio Nasica [another reading: Asina] and Rufus.
537 Geminus and Flaminius, in whose place Regulus was substituted.
538 Paulus for the 2nd time and Varro.
540 Fabius Maximus for the 2nd time and Marcellus.
554 Galba for the 2nd time and Cotta.
570 Pulcher for the 2nd time and Licinius.
579 Lepidus for the 2nd time and Scaevola.
589 Torquatus and Octavius (the same, On Ends, book 1, 24).
590 Torquatus for the 2nd time and Longinus.
592 Scipio Nasica and Figulus. In their place, because they had been elected with a flaw, Lentulus and Domitius are substituted.
596 Lepidus and Laenas for the 2nd time.
602 Marcellus for the 2nd time and Flaccus.
607 Scipio Aemilii [another reading: Aemilianus] and Drusus.
609 Maximus Aemilii [another reading: Aemilianus] and Mancinus.
612 Metellus for the 2nd time and Maximus (Cicero, Brutus, 161).
618 Philus and Servilius [another reading: Sex. Atilius].
624 Lentulus [another reading: App. Claudius] and Perperna.
625 Tuditanus and Anulius [Cicero, On the Nature of the Gods, 14: Aquilius].
626 Octavius and Rufus [another reading: T. Annius].
631 Metellus and Flamininus (Cicero, On His House, 136).
633 Opimius and Maximus Aemilii [another reading: Aemilianus].
637 Metellus Diadematus [or Dalmaticus] and Mucius Scaevola.
642 Drusus and Piso. In their consulship, the beginning of the Jugurthine War.
643 Nasica Scipio and Bestia Calpurnius (Cicero, Brutus, 128).
648 Serranus and Caepio. In their consulship Cicero was born, on the 8th day before the Kalends of May [3rd day before the Nones of January: Letters to Atticus 7.5].
650 Marius for the 2nd time and Fimbria.
651 Marius for the 3rd time and Orestes.
652 Marius for the 4th time and Catulus.
653 Marius for the 5th time and Aquillius.
654 Marius for the 6th time and Flaccus (Cicero, For Rabirius, 20).
655 Antonius and Albinus (Cicero, After His Return, to the Citizens, 11).
663 Philippus and Caesar [another reading: Sex. Julius Caesar].
664 Caesar [another reading: L. Julius Caesar I] and Lupus.
668 Marius for the 7th time and Cinna for the 2nd time. In their consulship Sallust was born, on the Kalends of October.
669 Cinna for the 3rd time and Carbo.
670 Carbo for the 2nd time and Scribonius [another reading: Cinna for the 4th time].
672 Carbo for the 3rd time and Marius (Cicero, Against Rullus 3, 7).
674 Sulla and Metellus Pius (Cicero, For Plancius, 69).
681 Marcus Lucullus and Cassius Longinus (Cicero, For Cluentius, 137).
685 Hortensius and Metellus (Cicero, For Cluentius). In their consulship Virgil was born, on the Ides of October.
686 Marcius Rex and Metellus (Cicero, Against Piso, 8).
688 Volcatius and Tullus. (He made two out of one. The colleague of Volcatius Tullus was Aemilius Lepidus (Cicero, Catilinarians 1, 15).)
690 L. Caesar and Figulus (Cicero, For Sulla, 56).
691 Cicero and Antonius. In their consulship the war of Catiline was waged.
694 Afranius and Metellus Celer (Cicero, Letters to Atticus 1, 15).
695 C. Caesar and Bibulus (Cicero, Against Piso, 3).
697 Lentulus and Metellus Nepos (Cicero, After his Return, in the Senate, 5).
698 Marcellinus and Philippus (Cicero, Letters to Friends 1, 9).
699 Pompey for the second time and Crassus for the second time.
702 Pompey for the third time and Metellus Scipio.
708 Caesar for the third time and Lepidus.
709 Caesar for the fourth time, alone.
710 Caesar for the fifth time and Antonius.

711 Pansa and Hirtius. In their consulship Cicero died, on the fourth day before the Kalends of May. (He died on the seventh day before the Ides of December. So the author of the Dialogue on Orators reported, on the testimony of Tiro.)

713 Antonius Pietas and Isauricus. In their consulship the Isaurian war was waged, and Julius Caesar, deceived by a plan of the Senate, was killed in the Curia by Cassius and Brutus. After him Octavian was called Caesar Augustus. (It is clear enough that these things have been set here out of their place. Caesar was killed in the year 710, on the Ides of March. The name of Augustus, moreover, was given to Octavian in the year 727, as Dio and Censorinus testify.)
714 Calvinus for the second time and Pollio.
715 (Spanish Era 1) Rufus Censorinus [another reading: L. Marcius Censorinus] and Sabinus.
716 Pulcher and Flaccus. In their consulship Sallust died, on the third day before the Ides of May.
719 Cornificius and Pompeius Magnus [another reading: Sextus Pompeius]. In their consulship the War of the Runaway Slaves was waged.
720 Antonius for the second time and Libo. In their consulship Cicero died, killed on the fourth day before the Kalends of May. (Everyone sees that this must be struck out.)

721 Octavian Augustus for the second time and Paulus [another reading: Tullus]. In their consulship, in the first year of the Era, the course of the moon was discovered. (This should have been assigned to the year 716.)
722 Ahenobarbus and Sosius. (These were wrongly placed lower down in the manuscript.)
723 Octavian Augustus for the third time and Corbilius [another reading: Corvinus].
724 Octavian for the fourth time and Crassus.
725 (Spanish Era 10) Octavian for the fifth time and Pulcher [another reading: Apuleius].
726 Octavian for the sixth time and Agrippa for the second time. In their consulship Carthage received its freedom from the Roman people.
727 Octavian for the seventh time and Agrippa for the third time.
728 Octavian for the eighth time and Taurus.
729 Octavian for the ninth time and Silanus.
730 Octavian for the tenth time and Flaccus.
731 Octavian for the eleventh time and Piso.
732 Aeserninus and Arruntius. Celsus and Hiburus. (These are wrongly inserted here.)

736 The two Lentuli. In their consulship Virgil died, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of October. (He died in the year immediately before, in the consulship of Saturninus and Lucretius, on the Ides of October.) Lentulus and Cornelius. (These are the two Lentuli just named, and it is not another consulship.)
742 Messala and Quirinus. Rubellius and Saturninus. (Inserted at random.)
744 Africanus [another reading: Fabius M. Africanus] and I. Antonius and Maximus.
747 Nero for the second time and Piso for the second time.
749 Octavian for the twelfth time and Sulla.
752 Octavian for the thirteenth time and Silanus [another reading: Silvanus]. In their consulship Christ was born, on the eighth day before the Kalends of January.
753 Lentulus and Piso. (From here on we shall write in the margin the years of the Christian Era; when 753 years are added to them throughout, they will give the years from the founding of the City.)
2 (Spanish Era 40) Vindicius [another reading: Vinicius] and Varus.
5 Magnus Pompeius [another reading: Cinna Magnus] and Valerius.
12 (Spanish Era 50) Omitted: Germanicus Caesar and C. Fonteius Capito.
13 Flaccus and Silanus [another reading: Plancus and Silius].
14 The two Sexti, Pompeius Magnus and Apuleius.
18 Tiberius Caesar for the second time and Drusus Germanicus [another reading: Germanicus Caesar] for the second time.
21 Tiberius Caesar for the third time and Drusus Germanicus for the third time [another reading: Drusus, son of Tiberius, for the second time].
25 Agrippa for the second time and Lentulus Galva [so the manuscript].

29 Rufus [another reading: Fusius, or Fufius, and Rubellius] and Rubellio. In their consulship Christ suffered, on the tenth day before the Kalends of April, and rose again on the eighth day before the same Kalends. [Here in the margin of the manuscript the following is read: Since the Gospel of John teaches that our Saviour and Lord taught for three years after his baptism, to which he came in the thirtieth year of his age, as is recorded under the reign of Tiberius Caesar. In this place there is an error of years through the consuls, unless the reckoning from Rufus and Rubellio is extended to the third pair of consuls.]
31 Tiberius Caesar for the fourth time, alone [another reading: and Aelius Sejanus].
32 (Spanish Era 70) Arruntius [another reading: A. Vitellius] and Ahenobarbus.
33 Galba -libolus [another reading: Sulpicius Galba] and Sulla.
34 Persicus and Vitellius Putus [another reading: L. Vitellius]. (In the manuscript it is assigned to the year 32.)
36 Aemilianus [another reading: Galienus, or Allienus] and Plautius.
39 Caesar [another reading: Gaius Caesar] for the second time and Caesianus.
40 Caesar for the third time, alone.
41 Caesar for the fourth time and Antoninus [another reading: Saturninus].
42 (Spanish Era 80) Claudius for the second time and Largus.
43 Claudius for the third time and Vitellius for the second time.
44 Crispus [another reading: Crispinus] for the second time and Taurus.
47 Claudius for the fourth time and Vitellius [another reading: L. Vitellius] for the third time.
48 Vitellius for the fourth time (Not the fourth time: for this is A. Vitellius) and Publicola.
51 Claudius [another reading: Claudius for the fifth time] and Orfitus.
52 (Spanish Era 90) Sulla and Cato [another reading: Otho].
57 Nero for the second time and Piso.
58 Nero for the third time and Messala Corvinus. In their consulship Peter and Paul suffered, on the third day before the Kalends of July.
60 Nero for the fourth time and Lentulus.
62 (Spanish Era 100) Marius and Gallus. In their consulship Judaea was captured.
68 Italicus and Trachalus. In their consulship Nero disappeared.
69 Galba for the second time and Titus Rufinus.
70 Vespasian for the second time, alone [another reading: and Titus Caesar for the first time].
71 Vespasian for the third time and Nerva.
72 (Spanish Era 110) Vespasian for the fourth time and Titus for the second time.
73 Domitian for the second time and Messalinus.
74 Vespasian for the fifth time and Titus for the third time.
75 Vespasian for the sixth time and Titus for the fourth time.
76 Vespasian for the seventh time and Titus for the fifth time.
77 Vespasian for the eighth time and Domitian for the third time [another reading: Titus for the sixth time, to whom Domitian was substituted]. In their consulship the Jews were utterly defeated.
79 Vespasian for the ninth time and Titus for the sixth time [another reading: Titus for the seventh time].
80 Titus for the seventh time and Domitian for the fourth time [another reading: Titus for the eighth time and Domitian for the seventh time].
82 (Spanish Era 120) Domitian for the fifth time and Flavius Sabinus.
83 Domitian for the sixth time and Rufus.
84 Domitian for the seventh time and Appius Sabinus for the second time.
85 Domitian for the eighth time and Fulvius.
86 Domitian for the ninth time and Dolabella.
87 Domitian for the tenth time and Saturninus.
88 Domitian for the eleventh time and Rufus.
90 Domitian for the twelfth time and Nerva for the second time.
92 (Spanish Era 130) Domitian for the thirteenth time and Saturninus.
93 Pompeianus and Priscianus [another reading: Pompeius and Priscus].
94 Asprenas and Lateranus [another reading: Arretinus Clemens].
95 Domitian for the fourteenth time and Clemens [another reading: T. Flavius Clemens].
96 Valens and Vetus. In their consulship Domitian died in the palace at Rome.
97 Nerva for the third time and Rufus for the third time.
98 Nerva for the fourth time and Trajan for the second time.
99 Palma and Senecio [another reading adds: for the second time].
100 Trajan for the third time and Pontinus [another reading: Fronto].
101 Trajan for the fourth time and Paetus.
102 (Spanish Era 140) Severianus and Syrius [another reading: Senecio for the third time and Sura].
103 Trajan for the fifth time and Maximus.
104 Suburanus [another reading: Suranus for the second time] and Marcellus.
105 Candidus for the second time and Quadratus.
107 Syra for the third time [another reading: Sura for the fourth time] and Senecio for the second time.
109 Palma for the second time and Tullus.
112 (Spanish Era 150) Trajan for the sixth time and Africanus. In their consulship, persecution of the Christians.
113 Celsus for the second time and Priscianus [another reading: Crispinus] for the second time.
118 Hadrian [another reading adds: for the second time] and Salinator.
119 Hadrian for the fourth time [another reading: for the third time] and Rusticus.
120 Severus for the second time and Fulvus.
121 Verus for the second time and Augur.
125 Asiaticus [another reading adds: for the second time] and Aquilinus.
126 Verus for the third time and Ambibulus.
129 Marcellus [another reading: Q. Julius Balbus] and Celsus.
132 (Spanish Era 170) Augurinus and Sergianus [another reading: Severianus].
134 Severus [another reading: Servilius, or Servianus] for the third time and Varus.
135 Pontianus and Aquilinus Rufus [another reading: Acilianus].
137 Caesar [another reading: Aelius Caesar] for the second time and Balbinus.
139 Antoninus for the second time and Praesens.
140 Antoninus for the third time and Aurelius.
141 Severus and Silvanus [another reading: M. Paeduceus Priscinus].
145 Antoninus for the fourth time and Aurelius for the second time.
146 Clarus [another reading adds: for the second time] and Severus.
148 Torquatus [another reading adds: for the second time] and Julianus.
152 (Spanish Era 190) Glabrio for the second time and Humilius [another reading: Omullus Verianus].
161 Antoninus for the fifth time and Aurelius Caesar, the two Augusti. In their consulship a persecution arose, and Polycarp and Pionius suffered.
162 (Spanish Era 200) Rufinus [another reading: Rusticus] and Aquilinus.
167 Verus for the third time and Quadratus.

288 Maximian for the second time and Anuarinus [another reading: Januarius].
290 Diocletian for the fourth time and Maximian for the third time.

293 Diocletian for the fifth time and Maximian for the fourth time.
294 Constantine [another reading: Constantius] and Maximian. In their consulship forts were built in Sarmatia opposite Aquincum and Bononia.
295 Tuscus and Anullinus. In their consulship the whole nation of the Carpi surrendered itself into Romania (Roman territory).
296 Diocletian for the sixth time and Constantius for the second time.
297 Maximian for the fifth time and Maximian for the second time. In their consulship the Persians were defeated.
298 Faustus for the second time and Gallus.
299 Diocletian for the seventh time and Maximian for the fifth [another reading: sixth] time. In their consulship the Marcomanni were defeated.
300 Constantius for the third time and Maximian for the third time.
301 Titianus for the second time and Nepotianus.
302 (Spanish Era 340.) Constantius for the fourth time and Maximian for the fourth time. In their consulship the emperors ordered that there be low prices.
303 Diocletian for the eighth time and Maximian for the seventh time. In their consulship [there was] the persecution of the Christians.

304 Diocletian for the ninth time and Maximian for the eighth time. In their consulship Diocletian and Maximian laid down the purple, becoming private men, and invested Severus and Maximian [another reading: Maximinus]. For Constantius and Maximian, who had been Caesars, were proclaimed Augusti in the same hour, on the day of the Kalends of April.
305 Constantius for the fifth time and Maximian for the sixth [another reading: fifth] time.

306 Omitted: Constantius for the sixth time and Maximian for the sixth time. In their consulship Constantius died, and afterwards Constantine was raised [as emperor] on the 8th day before the Kalends of August.
307 [Maximian] for the ninth time and Constantine. In their consulship, which is after the sixth consulship, Severus was killed at Rome.

308 Likewise [Maximian] for the tenth time and Maximian for the seventh time [another reading: Maximian for the ninth time]. In their consulship, which is [that of] Maxentius and Romulus, Licinius was raised [as emperor] at Carnuntum on the 3rd day before the Ides of November.

309 After the consulship [of the] tenth and seventh [another reading: the tenth of Maximianus Herculius and the seventh of Galerius Maximianus]. In their consulship, which is [that of] Maxentius for the second time and Romulus for the second time.
310 The second year after the consulship [of the] tenth and seventh. In their consulship, which is [that of] Maxentius alone for the third time, Maximian the elder died.
311 Maximian consul for the eighth time. In their consulship, which is [that of] Rufinus and Volusianus, Maximian the younger died.

312 (Spanish Era 350.) Constantine for the second time and Licinius for the second time. In their consulship, which is [that of] Maxentius alone for the fourth time, Maxentius was defeated and killed at Rome at the Milvian Bridge.
313 Constantine for the third time and Licinius for the third time.
314 Volusianus for the second time and Annianus. In their consulship the battle of Cibalae took place on the 8th day before the Ides of October.
315 Constantine for the fourth time and Licinius for the fourth time.
316 Sabinus and Rufinus. In their consulship Diocletian died at Sola [another reading: Salona] on the 3rd day before the Nones of December.
317 Gallicanus and Bassus. In their consulship three Caesars were raised, Crispus, Licinius and Constantine, on the day of the Kalends of March.
318 Licinius for the fifth time and Crispus Caesar. In their consulship there was darkness during the day at the ninth hour.
319 Constantine for the fifth time and Licinius Caesar.
320 Constantine for the sixth time and Constantine Caesar.
321 Crispus for the second time and Constantine for the second time.

324 Crispus for the third time and Constantine for the third time. In their consulship [there was] the battle of Hadrianople on the 5th day before the Nones of July, and the battle of Chalcedon on the 14th day before the Kalends of October, and Constantine [another reading: Constantius] was raised [as] Caesar on the 6th day before the Ides of November.
325 Paulinus and Julianus. In their consulship Licinius was killed.

326 Constantine for the seventh time and Constantine [another reading: Constantius] Caesar. In their consulship Crispus was killed, and Constantine Augustus celebrated his *vicennalia* (twentieth-anniversary games) at Rome.
329 Constantine for the eighth time and Constantine for the fourth time.
330 Gallicanus and Symmachus. In their consulship Constantinople was dedicated on the 5th day before the Ides of May.
332 (Spanish Era 370.) Pacatianus and Hilarianus. In their consulship the Goths were defeated by the Roman army in the lands of the Sarmatians on the 12th day before the Kalends of May.
333 Dalmatius and Zenophilus. In their consulship Constans was raised [as Caesar] on the 8th day before the Kalends of January.
334 Optatus and Paulinus. In their consulship the slaves of the Sarmatians, the whole nation, drove their masters out into Romania (Roman territory).

335 Constantius and Albinus. In their consulship Constantine Augustus celebrated his *tricennalia* (thirtieth-anniversary games) on the 8th day before the Kalends of August, and Dalmatius was raised [as] Caesar on the 14th day before the Kalends of October.

337 Felicianus and Titianus. In their consulship Constantine Augustus was taken away to the heavenly kingdom on the 2nd day before the Kalends of June, and in that same year three Augusti were proclaimed, Constantine, and Constantius, and Constans, on the 5th day before the Ides of September.
339 Constantius for the second time and Constans.
340 Acindynus and Proculus. In their consulship Constantius [another reading: Constantine] the younger was killed.

341 Marcellinus and Probinus. In their consulship a battle was fought with the nation of the Franks by Constans Augustus in the Gauls, and in that same year there was an earthquake in the East throughout the whole year, except at Antioch.

342 (Spanish Era 380.) Constantius for the third time and Constans for the second time. In their consulship the Franks were defeated or pacified by Constans Augustus; Hermogenes was dragged [to death].
346 Constantius for the fourth time and Constans for the third time.
348 Philippus and Salia. In their consulship there was the Persian war [fought] by night.

350 Sergius and Nigrinianus. In their consulship Constans was killed in the Gauls by Magnentius, and Magnentius was raised [as emperor] on the 15th day before the Kalends of February, and Vetranio at Sirmium on the Kalends of March in that year, and Nepotianus at Rome on the 3rd day before the Nones of June, and there was a great battle between the Romans and the Magnentians.

351 After the consulship of Sergius and Nigrinianus. In their consulship the battle with Magnentius took place at Mursa on the 4th day before the Kalends of October, and in that year Vetranio was deposed on the 8th day before the Kalends of January, and Constantius was raised [as] Caesar on the Ides of March [Chronicon Alexandrinum: on the Ides of March]; and the sign of the Saviour appeared in the East on the 3rd day before the Kalends of February, on the 28th day of the moon.
352 (Spanish Era 390.) Constantius for the fifth time and Constantius Caesar.

353 Constantius for the sixth time and Constantius for the second time. In their consulship Magnentius killed himself in the Gauls at Lugdunum on the 3rd day before the Ides of August, and Decentius, Magnentius' brother, hanged himself with a noose on the 15th day before the Kalends of September.
354 Constantius for the seventh time and Constantine [another reading: Constantius Gallus] for the third time. In their consulship Constantine Caesar was killed on the island of Flanona.
355 Arbitio and Lollianus. In their consulship Julian was raised [as] Caesar on the 8th day before the Ides of November.
356 Constantius for the eighth time and Julian Caesar. In their consulship the relics of the apostle Timothy entered Constantinople on the day of the Kalends of June.

In their consulship the relics of the holy apostles Andrew and Luke entered Constantinople on the 5th day before the Nones of March, and Constantius Augustus entered Rome on the 6th day before the Kalends of May, and celebrated his thirty-fifth [anniversary].

358 Datianus and Cerealis. In their consulship envoys of the Persians entered Constantinople on the 8th day before the Kalends of March. In that same year there was an earthquake, such that the city of the Nicomedians was overturned from its foundations on the 9th day before the Kalends of September; and another 150 cities were damaged in parts.

359 Eusebius and Hypatius. In their consulship Gratian, son of Valentinian Augustus, was born on the 14th day before the Kalends of May; and in that same year for the first time a prefect of the City entered office at Constantinople, named Honoratus, on the 3rd day before the Ides of December.
360 Constantius for the tenth time and Julian for the third time. In their consulship the Great Church was dedicated at Constantinople on the 15th day before the Kalends of March.

361 Taurus and Florentius. In their consulship Constantius Augustus died at Mopsucrenae, in the territory of Cilicia, a province of Phoenicia, on the 3rd day before the Nones of November, and Julian Augustus entered Constantinople on the 3rd day before the Ides of December.

363 Julian Augustus for the fourth time and Sallustius. In their consulship Julian Augustus was killed in the Persian war on the 6th day before the Kalends of July; and because he had become an apostate from God, and also a persecutor of Christians, he was killed, and the most Christian Jovian Augustus was raised on the 5th day before the Kalends of July.

364 Jovian Augustus and Varro [another reading: Varronianus]. In their consulship Jovian Augustus passed away at Dadastana on the 2nd day before the Kalends of March, and Valentinian Augustus was raised at Nicaea on the 5th day before the Kalends of March. In that same year Valens Augustus was raised at Constantinople, at the seventh milestone, on the tribunal, by his brother Valentinian, on the 4th day before the Kalends of April.

365 Valentinian and Valens, Augusti. In their consulship the sea went out beyond its bounds on the 3rd day before the Kalends of August; and in that same year a night robber and public enemy appeared within the city of Constantinople on the 4th day before the Kalends of October.

366 Gratian Nobilissimus [another reading: the most noble boy] and Dagalaifus. In their consulship Valentinian the Younger, son of Augustus Valens, was born on the 15th day before the Kalends of February; and in that same year the same public enemy and brigand was overwhelmed and destroyed by Augustus Valens within Phrygia Salutaris, on the plains of the Nacolians, on the 6th day before the Kalends of June. In that same year Augustus Valentinian thoroughly defeated the Alamannic people.

367 Lupicinus and Jovinus. In their consulship, in the city of Constantinople, God rained hail like stones on the 4th day before the Nones of July; and in that same year Gratian Augustus was raised in Gaul, at Amiens, on the tribunal, by his father Augustus Valentinian, on the 9th day before the Kalends of September.

368 Valentinian for the second time and Valens for the second time. In their consulship there was an earthquake, so that the city of the Nicaeans was levelled to the ground, on the 5th day before the Ides of October.

369 Valentinian Nobilissimus and Victor. In their consulship the magnificent work of the cistern of Constantinople was completed by Domitius Modestus, *vir clarissimus*, prefect of the City for the second time, which he had begun in his first prefecture. After seventeen years the contest was restored by Augustus Valens.

370 Valentinian for the third time and Valens for the third time. In their consulship there was a great famine in the parts of Phrygia; and the holy church where the blessed apostles were laid was dedicated on the 5th day before the Ides of April.
371 Gratian Augustus for the second time and Probus.
373 Valentinian for the fourth time and Valens for the fourth time.
374 Gratian for the third time and Aequitius [another reading: Equitius].

375 After the consulship of Gratian for the third time and Aequitius. In their consulship the Baths of Carosa were dedicated, the prefect Vindaonius Magnus, *vir clarissimus*, then being in office. And in that same year Valentinian the elder died on the 15th day before the Kalends of December at the fortress of Brigetio; and Valentinian the younger, son of Augustus Valentinian, was raised Augustus by the army on the tribunal on the 10th day before the Kalends of December in the city of Aquincum.

376 Valens Augustus for the fifth time and Valentinian the younger, Augustus. In their consulship the Goths were defeated and driven out by the people of the Huns, and were received into Romania out of mercy, by the command of Augustus Valens. And in that same year the body of Augustus Valentinian entered Constantinople on the 5th day before the Kalends of January.

377 Gratian for the fourth time and Merobaudes. In their consulship the people of the Goths, who had been received out of mercy, rebelled against the Romans; counts were sent with soldiers to subdue them, and they fought with the Goths.

378 Valens for the sixth time and Valentinian for the second time. In their consulship Valens Augustus entered Constantinople from the East on the 3rd day before the Kalends of June. And in that same year Valens Augustus set out from the city to the camp on the 3rd day before the Ides of June; and there was a great battle between the Romans and the Goths at the twelfth milestone from Adrianople, on the 5th day before the Ides of August. From that day Valens Augustus was nowhere seen; and for the whole year the Goths dwelt together throughout the diocese of Thrace, Scythia and Moesia, and plundered them; then they came right up to the gates of the city of Constantinople.

379 Ausonius and Olybrius. In their consulship Theodosius Augustus was raised by Augustus Gratian on the 14th day before the Kalends of February in the city of Sirmium. In that same year the Romans fought many wars with the Goths. Then victories were announced over the Goths, Alans and Huns on the 15th day before the Kalends of December. [In the margin of our manuscript the following is written, which Sirmond omitted: In their consulship Theophilus, bishop of Alexandria, wrote the table given below on the observance of Easter.]

380 Gratian Augustus for the fifth time and Theodosius Augustus. In their consulship victories of both Augusti were announced. And in that same year Theodosius A[ugustus] entered Constantinople on the 18th day before the Kalends of December.

381 Syagrius and Eucherius. In their consulship Athanaric, king of the Goths, entered Constantinople on the 3rd day before the Ides of January. In the same month the same Athanaric died, on the 8th day before the Kalends of February.

382 (Spanish Era 420.) Antonius and Syagrius. In their consulship Theodosius Augustus laid the body of Augustus Valentinian in a sarcophagus on the 9th day before the Kalends of March. In that same year the whole people of the Goths with their king surrendered themselves into Romania on the 5th day before the Nones of October.

383 Merobaudes for the second time and Saturninus. In their consulship Arcadius Augustus was raised at Constantinople, at the seventh milestone, on the tribunal, by Theodosius Augustus his father, on the 17th day before the Kalends of February. And in that same year the body of Constantia, daughter of Augustus Constantine, entered Constantinople on the 2nd day before the Ides of September.

384 Richomeres and Clearchus. In their consulship envoys of the Persians entered Constantinople. In that same year Honorius Nobilissimus was born in the purple on the 5th day before the Ides of September.

386 Honorius Nobilissimus and Evodius. In their consulship the people of the Greuthungi were defeated and subdued, and brought captive into Romania, by our [emperors] Theodosius and Arcadius; then they entered Constantinople with victory and triumph on the 4th day before the Ides of October.

387 Valerius [another reading: Valentinian] for the third time and Eutropius. In their consulship Arcadius Augustus celebrated his own *quinquennalia* (fifth-anniversary games) together with Theodosius Augustus his father, with shows and games, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of February.

388 Theodosius Augustus for the second time and Cynegius. In their consulship Cynegius, prefect of the East, died in his consulship at Constantinople. He restored all the provinces, worn down by long decay, to their former state, and made his way as far as Egypt, and overthrew the images of the pagans. Hence, with great grief of the whole people of the city, his body was escorted to the Apostles on the 25th day before the Kalends of April. And after a year his wife Achantia took him to Spain on foot. And in that same year the public enemy Maximus the tyrant was killed by Theodosius Augustus at the third milestone from Aquileia on the 5th day before the Kalends of August. And his son Victor too was killed a few days later in Gaul by a count of Theodosius Augustus.
389 Timasius and Promotus. In their consulship Theodosius Augustus entered the city of Rome with Honorius his son on the day of the Ides of June, and gave a largess to the Romans.
390 Valentinian for the fourth time and Neuterius [another reading: Neoterius].

392 [Spanish Era 430.] Arcadius Augustus for the second time and Rufinus. In their consulship Valentinian the younger was killed at Vienne, and Eugenius raised himself as tyrant. Afterwards Theodosius Augustus killed Eugenius.
393 Theodosius Augustus for the third time and
394 Arcadius Augustus for the third time and Honorius Augustus for the second time.
395 Olybrius and Probinus. In their consulship Theodosius Augustus passed away at Milan.
396 Arcadius Augustus for the fourth time and Honorius Augustus for the third time.
398 Honorius Augustus for the fourth time and Eutychianus. In their consulship Gildo was killed.

402 (Spanish Era 440.) Arcadius for the fifth time and Honorius for the fifth time. In their consulship an eclipse of the sun occurred on the 3rd day before the Ides of November.
404 Honorius for the sixth time and Aristo [another reading: Aristaenetus]. In their consulship there was civil war from the 3rd day before the Kalends of September.
405 Stilicho for the second time and Anthemius.

406 Arcadius for the sixth time and Probus.
407 Honorius for the seventh time and Theodosius Augustus for the second time.

416 Theodosius for the seventh time and Palladius.
417 Honorius for the eleventh time and Constantius for the second time.
418 Honorius for the twelfth time and Theodosius for the eighth time.

420 Theodosius for the ninth time and Constantius for the third time.
422 [Spanish Era 460.] Honorius for the thirteenth time and Theodosius for the tenth time.
423 Marinianus and Asclepiodotus. In their consulship the emperor Honorius died at Ravenna. (Up to here Sirmond's edition; the rest from the same manuscript.)
425 Theodosius for the eleventh time and Valentinian Caesar.
426 Theodosius for the twelfth time and Valentinian Augustus for the second time.
427 Pierius and Artabus [another reading: Hierius and Ardabur].
430 Theodosius for the thirteenth time and Valentinian for the third time.
433 Theodosius for the fourteenth time and Maximus.

437 Aetius for the second time and Segisvultus.

446 Aetius for the third time and Symmachus.
450 Valentinian for the seventh time and Avienus.
452 (Spanish Era 490.) Herculanus and Parracius [another reading: Sporatius].
454 Aetius for the fourth time and Studius.
455 Valentinian for the seventh time and Anthemius.
456 Avitus Augustus, consul [another reading: John and Varanes].
458 Ricimer and [Patricius], who [was named] from the East. (These belong to the year 459.)
